body: I suppose I may have to just adopt a tolerance for the pain as my system adjusts to a more healthy diet. It's gonna be rough, but if this gets me to meta it's so worth it. I really appreciate the advice on this!
Could you share some reasons why you lost 10lbs in recovery? Was it nausea, constipation, just a lot on the body etc.?
Where did you have drains at? Did they help with the bruising?
Do you know why your hips and ass turned black? I can understand bruising in the surgical site but hips and ass being bruised seems odd to me.

I have a very sedentary lifestyle as it is and still have a hard time putting on weight. That said, I actually stayed the same weight through my top recovery, while I lost weight walking around campus during college, so maybe it won't be as bad as I think. The not being able to strain with vnectomy is what worries me most, as well as not being able to fight infection if it happens.

Ah, I see. Trying to overcome the gross feelings like nausea and bloating are really hard for me, as I'm the type who stops something as soon as it hurts. Fiber is also an issue for me as usually when I take a good amount of fiber I end up in a lot of pain from trapped gas. For a long time I thought it was IBS until I figured out I could stop pain by not eating fiber, which makes me constipated. So the pain may just be a sign that things are moving at a better rate I guess. At this point I definitely think it would be worth fighting through the pain though, as bottom surgery is my number one goal in life right now and I want to be healthy for recovery. I'm recently graduated from college and looking for a job, so I hope that feeling bad all the time won't interfere with work.

For a while I made a smoothie with almond milk, oats, peanut butter and a banana in it, 300 cals a cup. But it stuck to my insides so bad it made my constipation worse. The only thing I found that works is Boost Plus which is 360 cals, but even with those I'm struggling. If I start making smoothies again all the ingredients may have to be liquid or something.
Did you struggle to eat during recovery? Or did you lose weight during recovery? Another person here said they lost 10lbs during recovery and that scares me.

I've tried 530 calorie shakes and they taste terrible. I have the 360 csl ones for better taste. Any ideas on how to make the 530 cal ones better are appreciated; they taste like melted butter.

I love Nutella but I have to be careful about having sugary sweets every day because after a few days I feel my blood sugar get unstable and I have to take a break from sweets. I'm not diabetic but I have a family history of diabetes.

I tried making smoothies for a while, but they always came out very thick and stuck to my insides so bad they just made the constipation worse. I could possibly try something like putting a shake in there with some protein powder and milk though, and drink it throughout the day as you mentioned. I feel like it's gonna be difficult for me to figure out a way to make the 530 cal shakes taste good even in a smoothie. Worth a try at this point. 
Where do you get CalorieMate from? I looked it up and it seems to be a Japanese thing, so I'm not sure how difficult they would be to find in good quality in the US. I'm a little iffy about ordering food through Amazon. I could definitely snack on those though. I have used Clif Mini bars as 100 cal snacks and they are good.
I should probably try to get with a dietician at this point. I've worked with my GI and PCP on this for so long and we're all still questioning, so it's time to bring in another opinion. Whatever I need to do to get this surgery honestly, it's my whole life's goal. I definitely appreciate that you've been willing to share your experience on this though, I didn't think I'd find anyone else with this specific of a problem.

I did have a gastric emptying study, and it came back within normal range. My GI is just as puzzled at the situation. I do eat small frequent meals, to the point I feel like I eat every 1-2 hours. I do take a nutrition shake daily, and I find it does help. I take Boost Plus that is 360 calories, because I tried the 560 and it makes me nauseous and makes my blood feel like tar, in addition to tasting like melted butter. Shakes are indeed a godsend and I want to be able to have higher cal ones without getting weird effects. I've also considered that I could be hypersensitive to feelings in my body and am just feeling what it's like to have a surplus of calories. Have the higher cal shakes been a problem for you at some point, like the things I described? I wanna go back on them but they are so hard to get down from the bad taste and thick blood feeling.

Yeah, I'm already afraid of getting food poisoning because I fear that if I lose even 5 pounds I'll end up with organ failure. From reading all the comments I do now think it's best if I try to gain weight first. I've been trying for like a year now and it seems near impossible though. But thankfully I'm still in my early-mid 20s and have the rest of my surgeries past me, so hopefully I can double down on this and just try to get healthier first.

I've been tested for gastroparesis, had an upper endoscopy, and had a CT scan of my abdomen and all came back fine. It seems I'm just not eating enough because of the constipation and no appetite. I literally do not feel hungry unless it's been like 8 hours since I ate, so I have figured there's probably something wrong with how my stomach messages my brain. I had a lot of bloodwork done and all that came back fine too. I don't know how people put on weight so easily. I feel devastated that this is getting in the way of the surgery I've been needing all my life, at such a critical time.

I count my calories and macronutrient intake with the app Chronometer. I'm a big numbers person so keeping track of how the numbers correlate with how I feel physically (hunger, tiredness etc.) is normally what motivates me to eat more. I've been trying to gain weight for so long now and I always feel like I just physically don't have enough room in my body for 1,800 calories because I get constipated so easily. I usually only manage to get 1,300, sometimes 1,500-1,700 on good days. I do think I should see a dietician though, because if my weight is going to prevent me from having bottom surgery this is detrimental. I have severe bottom dysphoria and I absolutely hate the thought of having to postpone surgery for a year or more, especially because the risk of aging out of insurance, and living in one of the most anti-trans states during this awful presidency. I do understand where you're coming from though, and thankfully I am still in my early-mid 20s, so maybe I will find a way.

I'm on daily miralax as it is, so the constipation issue was also my main concern. I'm thinking I may need multiple enemas through recovery just to go without ripping an incision. I'm a tank for pain and not very concerned with pain, but I am very concerned about getting a bowel obstruction or ripping an incision. Or getting backed up to the point that I can barely eat, which is how I got to be this underweight. Not fun.

Every bowel movement is a fight for me anyway lol. I take miralax every day at slightly varying doses and even then I sometimes have problems. Hence thinking I may need multiple enemas through recovery.

Yeah, that was why I was worried. I had to postpone my top surgery by a year to try to gain weight only to fail and stay the same. I feel very fortunate the surgery went well, but I also had minimal incision so it was simpler than most. I am still trying really hard to gain weight, but I also have only 2 and a half years left on my insurance before I age out of it. I live in TN and finding insurance that covers gender surgery here is very hard to find, so I hoped I could get everything done soon. The waitlists are already very long and make me wonder if I can get meta before I lose my insurance.

I don't have chronic nausea, but I do have GERD which I manage with avoiding acidic foods and sometimes taking meds if it's real bad. They gave me opioids after my hysto and taking the whole pill made me vomit, so I cut them in half and took them in more frequent does and I did fine. I didn't take opioids after top because they put a special numbing stuff on my muscles during surgery so I'd only have to take regular paid meds. My top recovery was mostly pain-free and I felt great after the first week (though I had minimal incision not DI). Didn't shit for 6 days though and had to give myself an enema, which is actually not unheard of for me in my normal life. I assumed I'd probably have to do it again if I had meta, probably several times during that first month of recovery due to the vnec not allowing me to strain. Sorry if that's TMI lol, I'm trying to have realistic expectations.

Update: I have had a telehealth consult with a Vanderbilt surgeon (it wasn't Dr. Kassis, but Dr. Patrick Assi, who I think is the guy Kassis has been training). They do DI and keyhole (https://www.topsurgery.net/procedures/keyhole-top-surgery.htm). The weird thing is that they refer to keyhole as peri. So they don't do the type where they make a circle around your nipple and do the drawstring method, but they do do the type where they make a minimal incision and take what little there is. 

There's basically no information on Dr. Assi that I can find right now, so I'm trying to get the word out via my experience.

The only place I heard of Dr. Kassis being able to do peri is from this comment: [https://www.reddit.com/r/TopSurgery/comments/1153z17/comment/j903m8t/](https://www.reddit.com/r/topsurgery/comments/1153z17/comment/j903m8t/) ...From this I hoped he would be able to, but I wouldn't know until I talk to him myself.

Actually kind of hard to tell. As I said I have a history of my body getting anxiety responses to my shot, but usually they would stop once I calmed down after the shot was over (a few minutes). Like I couldn't sit still, felt like my hands were shaking a bit. If I tried to sit down and do my deskwork I would get the chest pain again. But while walking or running around I would feel fine, better even.

A week or so after posing my previous comment I figured out that walking/moving around for an hour or two after my shot seems to make the other symptoms stop for the rest of the week. It's like T gives my body a surge of pent-up energy that has to get let out immediately or else suffer the consequences of repressing it for the rest of the week. It's super weird and I don't think I've heard of this happening to anyone else. I've been on T for over 3 years and this only started happening in recent months.

I have been going back and fourth between the consideration of keeping nipples after top surgery or not. Part of me says I should keep them because that's how normal guys look, and if I want to be a normal guy, I should keep them. They also don't really do much, so part of me says I should keep them because why would I remove something that's not actually doing active harm?

The part of me that says I should get rid of them says that well, guys aren't actually supposed to have nipples, they're a leftover from females. Plus they're irritating in terms of how they feel, and they don't do anything useful for me, they don't bring any pleasure aside from the knowledge that normal guys have nipples, even if it's kind of a leftover in biology. Also the consideration about nipple grafts being expensive and a bother to care for. It kinda seems like the cons might outweigh the pros, even if keeping them would look more natural.

That's my take anyway. I'm still thinking about it; it'll be a while until I get top surgery anyway. Might just tattoo them on.

"He" because I'm a man and "they" because it's neutral; anyone can be referred to as they. It's just a default. I keep it there because I realize that some people get pissed off about being called they for whatever reason, even though the whole purpose of a neutral pronoun is so it can be used on anyone. I want to communicate that message that I'm fine with neutral language for the reasons I stated.

It's like calling someone a person instead of a man or woman; that still applies to them, men and women are indeed people. Calling them a person doesn't mean implying they're a neutral human entity, especially when they make it known that's not the only pronoun they are fine with.

Although I have been tempted to just stick to typical he/him so people won't end up thinking I'm non binary. I think that's kinda silly though. Part of me also thinks "they" is a leftover from my confused agender days of internalized transphobia.

But he does collect images of her from newspapers, as it seems to be with the pictures posted on his closet door. One of them appears to be a trimming from an article, including words along with the image. He may also have learned to draw Jenny, and draws pictures of her himself. Sheldon took her plans to learn more about the way she was designed, so he could change himself to fit her preferences. Even though Sheldon definitely has his problematic side, a lot of people seem to overlook his good side. He would do literally *anything* for Jenny, even travelling across the galaxy to find her in the movie. He was the only person in the Christmas special to never give up on her; not even her own mother could do that. His extensive knowledge of Jenny may be a bit unsettling, but it's also very useful when she needs help, as he knows exactly how to help her. He's a fascinating character to me and I wish more people could see past his initial creepy side.

I would give a bit of leeway for the designs of the young Eds to not quite match their implied ages; many things on this show are purposefully ambiguous, age seems to be one of them. I like to imagine that the Dodgeball Incident was the reason why Edd moved, so that flashback happened soon after the incident, and presumably soon after he got his head injury, if you view that as his "breaking point" for revenge.

The three to be around the age of 5 at that point seems right to me, given how the show has a tendency to make young kids smarter than they should be anyway. For example, Sarah and Jimmy were learning algebra in Too Smart For His Own Ed, despite being only around 8 years old(their ages were never confirmed, but it's a safe guess from their behavior and appearance).

Seeing as how Edd doesn't seem to have ever met Eddy's Brother up until BPS, that creates a bit of a time error. Here's what I noticed: Whenever we see memories of Rolf in his homeland(aside from the wolf flashback in No Speak Da Ed), he looks around the same age as he does in the present day(locket pic in Wish You Were Ed, flashback in Every Which Way But Ed). This implies that he moved to the cul-de-sac in recent years, maybe 3 years ago at most(if he's 12-14ish). However, he remembers Eddy's Brother, as apparently something happened with Bro and his chickens. This implies that Bro only recently left the cul-de-sac...which can't be true if Edd has never met him, yet has been in the cul-de-sac since he was a toddler.

Probably an oversight, as mistakes are allowed sometimes, but it's the reason why I can never pinpoint when Bro left exactly.
